To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) novel dry forests are characterized by low structural development, low species density, and high species dominance; (2) novel dry forest species density can be greater than native dry forest species density at the 1-h plot scale; and (3) novel dry forests tend to have fallen leaves with lower than average concentrations of manganese and sodium and with lower C/N ratios.

the ecology of dry forest species assemblage dynamics in the Caribbean, the influence of novel dry forests on ecosystem functioning, and the conservation of native species in highly degraded areas.
the effects of novel forests on the ecological functioning of dry forests and the conservation of native species.
the ecological and conservation implications of novel forests, and the role of novel forests as a bridge for restoration of degraded native forests.

the novel forests in dry forests in Puerto Rico and in the US Virgin Islands are not a threat to the biodiversity and functioning of native dry forests, but they are important to the biodiversity and conservation of native dry forests.
novel dry forests are an important component of the dry forest landscape, and their ecological and conservation implications are significant and need to be considered when managing dry forest lands.
novel dry forest ecosystems are a new and novel forest type with novel ecological characteristics that can contribute to forest functioning and biodiversity conservation.
